deals.description: Closing month (exact day not disclosed). Toll Brothers signed on 2026-04-21 to buy substantially all the assets and operations of Buffington Homes, a private builder in Fayetteville AR; Toll's 10-Q says it closed in May 2026, was accounted for as an asset acquisition and was not material. Price not disclosed. Brought about 1,500 owned or controlled home sites across nine active or coming-soon communities, priced from the $400,000s to over $1M. All Buffington employees joined Toll; partners Clay Carlton and Mike Lamberth stay to focus on land acquisition and development. Builder Advisor Group advised Buffington.
deals.map_impact: No top-100 row changes: Buffington is not ranked. Rank 9 Toll Brothers enters northwest Arkansas (Fayetteville / Bentonville) with about 1,500 lots.
deals.source_title: Toll Brothers 10-Q for the quarter ended 2026-07-31, Note 2 Acquisition (announcement terms from Toll release of 2026-04-21)

deals.description: Closing date. Stanley Martin completed its all-cash purchase of Nasdaq-listed United Homes Group at about $221M enterprise value, $1.18 per share; UHG became a wholly owned subsidiary and its stock stopped trading. Announced 2026-02-23, closed 2026-05-04 (Virginia Business reported the completion on 2026-05-04; the cited copy of the company release is dated 2026-05-05). UHG closed 1,192 homes in 2025 in Greenville, Spartanburg, Clemson, Columbia and Myrtle Beach SC and Augusta GA. Second Stanley Martin deal in a year after Windsor Homes (Sept 2025). Vestra Advisors advised UHG's special committee.
deals.map_impact: Rank 56 United Homes Group is now owned by rank 18 Stanley Martin (parent Daiwa House); the UHG row merges into Stanley Martin and UHG is no longer a public company. Adds South Carolina and Augusta volume to Stanley Martin.
deals.source_title: Augusta CEO (Georgia CEO staff report reproducing the company release): Stanley Martin Homes Completes Acquisition of United Homes Group (2026-05-05)

deals.description: Closing date. Sumitomo Forestry completed its all-cash purchase of NYSE-listed Tri Pointe Homes on 2026-05-14 (merger agreement dated 2026-02-13); Tri Pointe survived as an indirect wholly owned subsidiary of Sumitomo Forestry and deregistered its shares (SEC filing). Per trade press the price was $47.00 per share, about $4.5B; Tri Pointe keeps its brand, Irvine home office and management under CEO Doug Bauer; it had 160+ active communities, and with Sumitomo's five existing US builders the group expects about 15,000 US homes a year across 18 states against a 23,000-a-year 2030 goal. In November 2026 Sumitomo cut its 2026 US closings forecast to 12,705 (from 14,160) and called Tri Pointe synergies with its other US builders its top priority.
deals.map_impact: Rank 19 Tri Pointe Homes is no longer a listed company; it becomes a sister of rank 15 DRB Group (builder_id drb-group) (Sumitomo Forestry's other top-100 builder) and Sumitomo's other US builders. The Tri Pointe row stays as a separate brand but its parent changes to Sumitomo Forestry; combined Sumitomo US volume is roughly top-five scale. Leadership stayed. Watch for consolidation between Tri Pointe and the other Sumitomo builders in 2027.
deals.source_title: Tri Pointe Homes Form S-8 POS filed 2026-05-14 (merger with Sumitomo Forestry completed May 14, 2026); price and operating details from HousingWire 2026-05-14 and Builder and Developer 2026-05-21

deals.description: Announcement date; the release says Eastwood 'announced the acquisition' and Zelman, the seller's adviser, calls it a completed May sale. Price not disclosed. Peachtree is a private south-Atlanta builder; per Zelman the deal lifts Eastwood's Atlanta production from about 120 closings a year to about 350-400, and the seller's principals stay on as development partners. Most Peachtree operations stay with Eastwood, which now has 11 divisions; its second purchase in about 18 months after Napolitano Homes (Virginia, 2025). JTW Advisors advised Eastwood, Zelman Partners advised Peachtree.
deals.map_impact: No top-100 row disappears: Peachtree is outside the top 100. Rank 46 Eastwood Homes roughly triples its Atlanta volume and should move up a few places on closings.
deals.source_title: Metro Atlanta CEO (staff report reproducing the company release): Eastwood Homes Expands Further into Metro Atlanta Through Acquisition of Peachtree Building Group (2026-05-27)

deals.acquirer: Mungo Homes (Clayton Home Building Group / Berkshire Hathaway)
deals.description: Announcement date; the release says Mungo 'announced the acquisition' and gives no separate closing date. Price not disclosed. McGuinn builds in Aiken, Columbia, Greenville, Hilton Head and Sumter SC and Augusta and Savannah GA, has about 75 employees and was projected to close nearly 800 homes in 2026 (ResiClub puts 2025 closings at 993 and says build-to-rent has at times been the bulk of its business). Whelan Advisory advised McGuinn.
deals.map_impact: Rank 65 McGuinn Homes is absorbed into Mungo Homes, a Clayton Properties Group (rank 12) builder, so the McGuinn row disappears into Clayton and, after the Taylor Morrison roll-up, into the Berkshire site-built platform. Adds Augusta GA and Aiken SC and build-to-rent relationships. Founder Wade McGuinn sold; HousingWire reports McGuinn will become part of the Mungo platform rather than stay stand-alone.
deals.source_title: Mungo Homes: Mungo Homes Acquires McGuinn Homes, Expands Southeast Presence (2026-07-02)

deals.description: Closing date. Berkshire Hathaway completed its purchase of NYSE-listed Taylor Morrison for $72.50 per share in cash, about $6.8B equity value and $8.5B enterprise value; announced 2026-05-31, closed 2026-07-24. Sheryl Palmer stays CEO and will oversee integrating Taylor Morrison (incl. Esplanade, Yardly build-to-rent and Taylor Morrison Home Funding) with Berkshire's site-built operations in Clayton Properties Group (15 regional builders). Combined 2025 closings were nearly 23,000 across 21 states, 52 markets and 700+ communities.
deals.map_impact: Rank 6 Taylor Morrison is no longer public and now shares an owner with rank 12 Clayton Properties Group. Berkshire says Taylor Morrison will lead a unified site-built operation, and Taylor Morrison's CMO told ResiClub (2026-08-20) that all of Clayton's site-built builders will roll up under Taylor Morrison while manufactured/modular stays with Clayton Homes; so the two rows effectively become one Berkshire platform of about 23,000 closings, the 4th largest US builder (level with NVR). Sheryl Palmer leads it. acquirer_builder_id is null because Berkshire itself is not a ranked builder; its ranked subsidiary is clayton-properties-group.
deals.source_title: Taylor Morrison newsroom: Berkshire Hathaway Completes Acquisition of Taylor Morrison (2026-07-24)

deals.description: Closing date. Stanley Martin agreed on 2026-07-16 to buy employee-owned Florida builder Holiday Builders (Melbourne FL); the seller's adviser says it closed 2026-07-29 (other reports say it became official 2026-07-30). Price not disclosed. Holiday closed about 1,050 homes in 2025 and brings 40+ communities and about 10,600 controlled Florida lots (Palm Coast, Palm Bay, Panama City, Orlando area, North Port, Cape Coral). Holiday becomes a wholly owned subsidiary. Zelman Partners advised Holiday.
deals.map_impact: Rank 62 Holiday Builders is now owned by rank 18 Stanley Martin (Daiwa House); the Holiday row merges into Stanley Martin. With UHG, Stanley Martin's 2025 pro-forma closings are about 7,560 (5,320 + 1,192 + 1,050, a sum of the figures in the cited articles), and Daiwa House's US builders total about 10,000.
deals.source_title: HousingWire (sponsored, Zelman): Holiday Builders Sale Shows What Buyers Want in Homebuilder M&A (2026-07-29)

deals.target: Innovative Construction Group (ICG), a PulteGroup subsidiary
deals.description: Not a homebuilder purchase: a division sale by a top-3 builder. Announcement date. Builders FirstSource agreed to buy ICG, PulteGroup's off-site framing business (wall panels, roof and floor trusses, installation; plants of about 400,000 sq ft in Florida and about 200,000 sq ft in South Carolina), for an undisclosed price. Pulte bought ICG in 2020 for about $104M and said in January 2026 it would divest it; Pulte expects to keep buying off-site components without owning the factories. Closing date not confirmed in the sources opened (Vestra Advisors, Pulte's adviser, lists the deal under August 2026).
deals.map_impact: No ranking change. Rank 3 PulteGroup (seller, builder_id pultegroup) exits factory ownership and frees capital for homebuilding; relevant as a sign of a large builder going more asset-light.
deals.source_title: HousingWire: Why Builders FirstSource bought ICG; and why Pulte sold it (2026-08-03)

deals.description: Not an acquisition: open-market share purchases. Date is the report date. ResiClub reports from Berkshire's SEC filings that Berkshire raised its Lennar holding by 94% in Q3 2026 and by about 260% since the start of 2026, to around 11% of Lennar; an earlier ResiClub piece (2026-08-20) put the holding at 13.1M Class A shares plus Class B, worth just over $1.2B, with a small new D.R. Horton position of 3,600 shares. No bid for Lennar has been reported.
deals.map_impact: No row merges. The owner of the new Taylor Morrison / Clayton platform (ranks 6 and 12) is now also a roughly 11% shareholder of rank 2 Lennar, which matters for anyone reading Lennar's and Millrose's ownership and for speculation about further Berkshire housing moves.
deals.source_title: ResiClub: Warren Buffett's successor makes third big housing market bet this year, now owning around 11% of Lennar (2026-10-05)

deals.description: Announcement date; the release says Century 'has acquired' substantially all the assets of HistoryMaker, so announced and closed together. Price, lots and community counts not disclosed. HistoryMaker (founded 1949, Grapevine TX) builds only in Dallas-Fort Worth; the deal triples Century's DFW community count. Century's DFW operations and HistoryMaker combine into one division based in Grapevine with HistoryMaker division leadership joining; Century keeps a land development relationship with HistoryMaker's sister company Jabez Development. Vestra Advisors advised HistoryMaker.
deals.map_impact: Rank 77 HistoryMaker Homes is absorbed into rank 10 Century Communities; the HistoryMaker row disappears. HistoryMaker's division leaders run Century's combined DFW division; owner and CEO Nelson Mitchell sold, and Jabez Development continues as a land developer for Century.
deals.source_title: Century Communities Triples Dallas-Fort Worth Footprint with Acquisition of HistoryMaker Homes (PR Newswire release, 2026-10-08, as carried by Finviz)

deals.description: Closing date. Dream Finders completed its all-cash purchase of NYSE-listed Beazer at $33.50 per share, about $2.2B enterprise value (about $915M equity, roughly 0.8x book per trade press); Beazer delisted. It began hostile: private approaches from February 2026, a public $25.75 offer on 2026-05-11, raised to $29.25 on 2026-06-22 and $32.00 on 2026-07-08, each rejected or not accepted, then a definitive agreement on 2026-08-07; Beazer holders approved in mid-October and it closed 2026-10-20. Dream Finders expects $100M+ annual cost synergies, will move Beazer communities onto Dream Finders floor plans and aims to bring leverage back down within 18-24 months. Combined: about 520 communities in 26 markets.
deals.map_impact: Rank 21 Beazer Homes merges into rank 14 Dream Finders Homes; the Beazer row disappears and the combined company calls itself the 6th largest US builder (by 2025 revenue; HousingWire counts 13,035 combined 2025 closings). Adds California, Nevada, Indiana and Delaware and more Maryland/DC to Dream Finders. Patrick Zalupski stays CEO and co-chairman; Rick Beckwitt (ex-Lennar and D.R. Horton) joined the Dream Finders board as co-chairman in July 2026 during the bid. The closing release names no continuing role for Beazer CEO Allan Merrill or other Beazer executives.
deals.source_title: Dream Finders Homes Completes Acquisition of Beazer Homes (Business Wire release, 2026-10-20, as carried by Finviz)

'Consolidation Accelerates in Home Builder M&A Market') returned 403 to both fetch methods and was not read; businesswire.com, ir.beazer.com, streetinsider.com, eastwoodhomes.com, marketbeat.com and risewellhomes.com also blocked. Whelan Advisory and JTW Advisors sites rendered no deal text.

Purchase prices not publicly disclosed: Mungo/McGuinn, Stanley Martin/Holiday Builders, Century/HistoryMaker (also no lot or community counts), Eastwood/Peachtree, Toll/Buffington, Builders FirstSource/ICG.

Holiday Builders closing day: the seller's adviser (Zelman, in HousingWire sponsored content) says 2026-07-29; search snippets of other reports say it became official 2026-07-30. Not resolved against a Stanley Martin or Daiwa House release.

United Homes Group closing day: 2026-05-04 per Virginia Business and search results; the only full copy of the company release opened (Augusta CEO) is dated 2026-05-05. The BusinessWire original was blocked.
Beazer leadership after closing: no source opened says whether Allan Merrill or other Beazer executives stay with Dream Finders. Beazer's own closing 8-K was not read.

Berkshire/Taylor Morrison and Mungo/McGuinn: how and when the Clayton site-built builders are legally reorganised under Taylor Morrison is not public beyond the statements cited; no closing date separate from the 2026-07-02 announcement was found for McGuinn.

Deals announced before 2026-05-01 whose closing could fall in the window but was not confirmed: Hajime Construction (Iida Group) buying 51% of Utah's Wright Homes, announced 2026-03-10 (closing date not found); Trumark Homes (Daiwa House) / JK Monarch, announced 2026-03-20 and described by Builder and Developer as acquired in late March 2026, so treated as before the window. Both left to the Jan 2025-Apr 2026 agent, as are Invitation Homes/ResiBuilt (Jan 2026) and Taylor Morrison/Pyatt Builders lots (Feb 2026).

Rumored or terminated deals: none found beyond the rejected Dream Finders offers for Beazer (which ended in the agreed deal). KB Home and LGI Homes were named as possible targets in Barron's (June 2026, seen only as a search snippet) and in HousingWire commentary, but no approach or bid has been reported; not listed as a deal.

No new Sekisui House, Open House, Asahi Kasei, Misawa/Toyota Housing or private-equity purchase of a US homebuilder was found for May-Nov 2026. HousingWire (2026-10 and 2026-11-19) reports the Japanese-owned builders cutting US forecasts and expects less US deal-making from them; Sekisui House is unifying its US brands rather than buying.

Left out as too small or out of scope: McBride Homes (rank 76) buying the remaining Alder Creek Manors homesites in Wright City MO from Houston Homes (reported 2026-09-14, seen only as a search snippet); Champion Homes buying manufactured-home retailers Timberline Homes (announced 2026-10-05) and Homes Direct; CoStar's $800M purchase of Zonda, the publisher of the Builder 100 ranking (announced 2026-05-29, closed 2026-08-21); QXO/TopBuild; Reds10/MMY US.
